mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing or equivalent corporate status certificate of each direct or indirect corporate UBO
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent company registrar in the jurisdiction of corporate seat (e.g., Companies House, Delaware Division of Corporations, ACRA, Registrar of Companies)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (if the issuing jurisdiction is a Hague Apostille Convention party) or Consular Legalization through the Canadian embassy/consulate; certified translation required if the document is not in English or French

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized Power of Attorney or corporate authorization appointing the Canadian incorporator and registered office service provider
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public in the country of origin; corporate officer executing on behalf of the parent/UBO entity
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or Consular Legalization; attach certified English/French translation if the original is in another language

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified true copies of government-issued photographic identity documents for each director, officer, and individual with significant control (UBO)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: National passport/identity document issuing authority; copy certified by a notary public in the country of issuance
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarized copy; apostille/consular legalization of the notary's certificate if required by the receiving Canadian authority; certified translation of any non-English/French notation

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incumbency or Register of Directors evidencing the legal authority of signatories to approve incorporation and CBCA filings
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Corporate secretary or registered agent of the parent entity or corporate UBO
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarization plus Hague Apostille or Consular Legalization, with certified English/French translation if applicable

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all directors, officers, registered shareholders, UBOs, counterparties, and beneficial owners of payment processors against OFAC's Specially Designated Nationals and Blocked Persons List, the United Nations Security Council Consolidated List, Canada's Consolidated Autonomous Sanctions List (CASL), and designations under the Special Economic Measures Act and the Criminal Code terrorism financing provisions. Politically exposed persons (domestic or foreign PEPs, heads of international organizations, and their relatives/close associates) must be identified in accordance with FINTRAC guidance and, where identified, subjected to enhanced due diligence. Given the USDC payment rail proposed in the target commercial model, virtual currency wallet addresses and counterparties should be screened for OFAC and UN sanctions linkages; transaction monitoring for money laundering, terrorist financing, and proliferation financing indicators must be documented. Mere receipt of USDC for AI API access does not by itself make the entity a reporting entity under the PCMLTFA; however, if the corporation later exchanges, transfers, or administers virtual currency on behalf of third parties as a business, it must assess mandatory registration with FINTRAC as a money services business and implement a full AML/CFT program.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Corporations Canada Online Filing Centre (Canada.ca / Corporations Canada)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Corporate names may be in English, French, or bilingual. A name in a non-official language must be transliterated or translated into English or French for the NUANS search and registration. The name must be distinctive, not confusingly similar to existing names, and must include a prescribed corporate designator: 'Limited', 'Limitée', 'Incorporated', 'Incorporée', 'Corporation', 'Compagnie' or an abbreviation such as 'Ltd.', 'Ltée', 'Inc.', 'Corp.', or 'Co.'.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the proposed name is rejected by Corporations Canada as confusing, prohibited, or otherwise non-compliant, the applicant may submit a written reconsideration request to the Director under the CBCA name framework within 15 days of the refusal. The request must include a fresh NUANS report where applicable, evidence of distinctiveness, prior use, trademark registration, or consent from the holder of the conflicting name. If the Director maintains the refusal, the applicant may apply to the Federal Court for judicial review; legal counsel should be retained before commencing the court application. A valid name reservation may be extended for an additional 90-day period at the Director's discretion, provided the reservation has not lapsed and the incorporation filing is actively being completed.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Permitted for a registered office only if the virtual office provider supplies a physical address in the province designated in the articles and is able to receive and forward legal process. A post office box or general delivery address is not acceptable. For an ISIC 6201 AI/LLM API platform, no federal physical-operations mandate exists, so a registered office service provider is commercially viable and compliant.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low; estimated annual probability below 5% for unannounced Corporations Canada physical inspection of the registered office. FINTRAC compliance examinations are ordinarily scheduled and document-focused, but unscheduled site visits can occur under court warrant in the course of money laundering or terrorist financing investigations.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Canada Business Corporations Act (CBCA), R.S.C. 1985, c. C-44, ss. 5-6, 16, 101, 104-106, 113, 115, 189; and Canada Business Corporations Regulations, 2001, SOR/2001-512
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Corporations Canada, Innovation, Science and Economic Development Canada (ISED)
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Articles of Incorporation (Form 4001), together with Notice of Registered Office (Form 4003) and Notice of Directors (Form 4006)
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No minimum paid-up capital required under the CBCA; no escrow account is prescribed. Authorized share capital is fixed by the articles, and subscription proceeds are allocated as paid-up capital upon allotment.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: FIRST BOARD RESOLUTION: The board of directors unanimously resolves and approves: (1) the subscription and allotment of common shares to the incorporators in accordance with Schedule A to the Articles; (2) the adoption of the registered office located in the Province/Municipality and the designation of that address as the corporate seat; (3) the appointment of Chief Executive Officer, Chief Financial Officer and Secretary, each to serve until successor appointment; (4) the adoption of the draft by-laws as the corporation's by-laws; and (5) the authorization of officers to open bank accounts and execute procedural documents.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Corporations Canada, Innovation, Science and Economic Development Canada
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit a NUANS Name Search Request through Corporations Canada's online portal or an accredited service provider. Confirm that the proposed corporate name is distinctive, legal, and does not conflict with existing registered marks. Reserve the name for 90 days if immediate filing is not possible.
required_dossiers: Proposed corporate name (up to three alternatives)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected, amend the proposed name and file a new NUANS request, or elect to incorporate under a numbering company name (e.g., 0000000 Canada Inc.).

step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the Articles of Incorporation, including share structure and directors' information. Ensure the registered office is situated in Canada. At least 25% of directors must be resident Canadians for public corporations; for private corporations, a majority must generally be resident Canadians unless an exemption applies. Complete Form 4003 and Form 4006.
required_dossiers: Consent to act as director forms
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Exchange deficient notices or amend draft articles prior to filing; if rejected, correct the disclosed information and resubmit the documents.

step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Log in to Corporations Canada's online portal, upload the prepared forms, and pay the statutory filing fee using a credit card or interac. Electronically attest to the accuracy of the information and submit the application. Retain the transaction confirmation number.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the application is queried, respond to the deficiency request within 30 days, amend the relevant form, and resubmit; if refused, request a director-level review of the decision.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Receipt of Certificate of Incorporation and CRA Registrations
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Retrieve the electronic Certificate of Incorporation and accompanying Business Number (BN). Immediately use the BN to register for GST/HST, payroll deductions, and corporate income tax account. Open a corporate bank account with the certificate and BN in hand.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the CRA registration cannot be effectuated, file Form RC1 separately. To replace a misplaced certificate, request a sealed certified copy from Corporations Canada.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: First Board Meeting and Organizational Compliance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Board of Directors / Corporate Minute Book
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Convene the first board meeting to formally adopt the by-laws, confirm the registered office, ratify bank account resolutions, approve share issuance to founders, and appoint officers. Record minutes in the corporate minute book and affix the corporate seal if adopted.
required_dossiers: Directors' consents and oaths of office
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If any consent form is missing, obtain it retrospectively; call an emergency board meeting to ratify all unapproved acts and correct minute omissions.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Director appointed under CBCA and provincial/municipal business licensing authorities having jurisdiction over the registered office
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Federal Certificate of Incorporation and applicable municipal business operating licence

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Environment and Climate Change Canada (ECCC) and provincial environmental protection ministry
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Registration (Class B) - exempt from full Environmental Impact Assessment for AI/LLM API platform operations with negligible physical discharges; subject to self-assessment under the Canadian Environmental Protection Act, 1999
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Compliance with clean water effluent limits for municipal wastewater, VOC emission thresholds for standby generators, and hazardous waste manifest requirements for electronic waste; lower-tier registration obligations for negligible atmospheric emissions

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certificate issued by municipal fire marshal, building occupancy clearance for structural load compliance, and workplace health and safety inspection under Part II of the Canada Labour Code

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) / Agence du revenu du Canada (ARC). Primary portals: CRA My Business Account (www.canada.ca/en/revenue-agency.html) and Business Registration Online; GST/HST NETFILE for electronic return filing. Customs border operations (export declarations) are administered by the Canada Border Services Agency (CBSA). Provincial sales taxes are separately administered by Revenu Quebec and provincial ministries.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A federally incorporated CBCA corporation automatically receives a 9-digit Business Number (BN) from CRA upon Corporations Canada online incorporation. Program accounts are then added via Business Registration Online, by telephone (1-800-959-5525), or by Form RC1: RC (corporate income tax), RT (GST/HST), RP (payroll), RD (import/export). A foreign parent establishing a subsidiary may pre-register with Form RC4601 (non-resident GST/HST) or RC1 submitted to CRA Summerside Tax Centre; processing takes 10-15 business days and CRA mails access codes within 5-10 days. Registration must precede Canadian payroll, GST/HST collection, or customs activity.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No US-style check-the-box regime; entity classification under the Excise Tax Act and Income Tax Act (ITA) is mandatory, and hybrid mismatch rules (ss.18.2, 18.3, 94B ITA) are non-elective. Relevant elections: non-calendar taxation year (s.249.1 ITA); capital dividend election (s.83(2)); paid-up capital increase election (s.89(11)); s.85 asset rollover; associated-corporation allocation; GST/HST s.156 election for closely related corporations; s.167 change-of-use election; quick method or simplified input tax credit election for registrants.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: GST/HST under Part IX of the Excise Tax Act: 5% federal GST; participating provinces apply HST (13% Ontario; 15% Nova Scotia, New Brunswick, Newfoundland and Labrador, Prince Edward Island); Quebec imposes 9.975% QST separately. A separate 3% Digital Services Tax applies to large digital businesses (global revenue over CAD 750M and Canadian digital services revenue over CAD 20M) retroactively from January 1, 2022, with the first return due June 30, 2025.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CAD 30,000 in annual worldwide taxable supplies (small-supplier threshold under s.148 ETA); zero-rated exports count toward this threshold. Non-resident digital service suppliers (including AI/LLM API platforms) providing specified digital supplies to Canadian recipients must register under the simplified GST/HST regime once Canadian-source taxable supplies exceed CAD 30,000 in the preceding four calendar quarters or current quarter (effective July 1, 2021). Registration is voluntary but recommended where all supplies are zero-rated, to recover input tax credits.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: None. Canada imposes no real-time fiscal clearance, mandatory digital stamping, or continuous transaction controls; e-invoicing is voluntary, with a federal PEPPOL-based e-invoicing pilot under the Pan-Canadian Trust Framework (2024-2025). Electronic filing of GST/HST returns via NETFILE is mandatory for registrants with annual taxable supplies exceeding CAD 1.5M. All books, records, invoices, and supporting export documentation must be retained for six years.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Cross-border AI/LLM API token and inference services supplied to a non-resident recipient qualify for 0% GST/HST under Schedule VI, Part V, ss.22-23 of the Excise Tax Act, provided: (i) the recipient is a non-resident person; (ii) the supply is not in respect of real property situated in Canada; (iii) the service is not performed in respect of tangible personal property situated in Canada at the time of performance; and (iv) the service is not consumed by an individual physically present in Canada. The zero-rating applies to both exported services and licensed intangible digital property; input tax credits on Canadian hosting, compute, office, and professional expenses remain fully recoverable with adequate export substantiation.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Executed master subscription agreement and order form identifying the non-resident customer and jurisdiction
Commercial invoice denominated in CAD expressly stating 0% GST/HST with zero-rating statutory reference
Inward remittance evidence: SWIFT MT103 credit advice, card scheme settlement statement, or USDC/stablecoin transfer receipt
Non-resident status certificate: certificate of residence, foreign incorporation certificate, or treaty residency attestation
API usage logs and token consumption records evidencing offshore service delivery
Where physical media or hardware is exported: Form B13A export declaration filed via the Canadian Export Reporting System (CERS) within 15 days of exportation, plus bill of lading
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: CRA may reassess within four years of the original assessment; the limitation period is unlimited for fraud, neglect, or willful default. Unsubstantiated zero-rating triggers retroactive GST/HST at 5%-15% with arrears interest and penalties: 10% under s.285.1 ETA or 50% under s.163(2) ITA for gross negligence; criminal evasion under ss.327 ETA and 239 ITA draws fines up to 200% of the tax and imprisonment. Failure to retain export records attracts a CAD 500 penalty per failure. Canada has no federal statutory 180-day FX repatriation deadline, but export receivables outstanding beyond one year may trigger deemed interest under s.17 ITA; a 180-day documentary repatriation covenant is therefore market standard and supports the export journal.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Canada, Department of Finance Canada, and the Financial Transactions and Reports Analysis Centre of Canada (FINTRAC); the Office of the Superintendent of Financial Institutions (OSFI) supervises federally chartered banks. Canada maintains no codified Foreign Exchange Control Act; the Canadian dollar floats freely under a market-determined exchange rate regime.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Canadian dollar (CAD) is fully convertible on both current and capital account transactions and Canada adheres to IMF Article VIII. Profit remittances, dividends, and capital repatriation are not subject to exchange control approval, conversion quotas, or central-bank permit layers. Frictions arise solely from non-FX regulatory domains: Part XIII withholding tax filings for dividends and royalties, CRS/FATCA reporting, FINTRAC large-transaction reporting for amounts equivalent to C$10,000 or more, and Canadian CFC attribution rules for passive foreign income of controlled foreign affiliates.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: There are no statutory export-proceeds surrender rules, mandatory conversion timelines, or minimum conversion ratios for export receipts in Canada. Exporters may retain foreign currency in permitted foreign-currency bank accounts, use their CAD earnings for operational liquidity, and enter into voluntary forward or swap contracts. The only obligations are contemporaneous financial recordkeeping, income tax recognition under Canadian GAAP/IFRS, and transfer-pricing compliance for intercompany export settlements.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: Low for a pure offshore electronic-money institution and Medium for a Canadian-registered money service business (MSB). An offshore EMI is not permitted to take deposits or hold CAD in Canada unless licensed as an authorized foreign bank branch; it may, however, be used as a payment-processor conduit for AI API subscription billing if supported by Stripe Canada as an MSB. Core treasury liquidity should reside in a Schedule I Canadian bank account, not in an off-Channel EMI wallet.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical in-branch appearance is not statutorily mandatory for a Federal business corporation whose directors complete enhanced due diligence. Banks may require a notarized identification package, director ID attestations, and one or more video-conference KYC interviews for a remote foreign-owned entity. For maximum certainty, the Canadian corporate secretary or a resident director should attend an in-person verification at the chosen bank branch before account activation.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Ultimate beneficial owner structure includes a holding entity in a jurisdiction with opaque ownership standards or a disregarded partnership in the United States.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Full organizational chart from individual to Feit; certificates of good standing; register of directors for every entity; notarized passports and utility bills for all UBOs holding 25% or more; registered office address verification; signed Canadian corporate attestation with tax identification numbers; and a resolution naming the first-deposit maker.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Commercial scope coding as high-volume, non-face-to-face generative AI API token sales triggers fraud and money-laundering red flags.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certificate of Federal incorporation; ISIC_6201 evidence with a contractual statement of offered services; SOC 2 Type 2 report or equivalent control framework; third-party identity verification policy for API customers; historical bank statements from the founding jurisdiction; and a written AML/transaction-monitoring compliance manual.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Use of cryptocurrency (USDC) as a target payment rail creates concerns under FINTRAC AML regulations.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Proof of USDC settlement through a FINTRAC-registered MSB in Canada or a licensed US entity; wallet-address KYB/KYC records; source-of-funds declarations; policy for suspicious transaction report (STR) filing; commercial contracts confirming the token purchase is a prepaid base; and transactional thresholds for onboarding high-value API customers.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Mismatch between the remitter of the capital injection and the legal beneficial owner of the receiving corporation.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Corporate resolution authorizing the capital contribution; signed share subscription agreements; beneficial-ownership schedule with >25% threshold identification; SWIFT MT103 copy annotated with the proper end-of-message reference; bank-to-bank attestation of source of funds; and any US Form K-1 or equivalent distribution confirmation if pass-through capital is used.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Non-resident equity and shareholder loans must be received via SWIFT MT103 into the Canadian operating account as final CAD value; the remitter should include a reference code such as 'EQUITY CONTRIBUTION' or 'SHARE SUBSCRIPTION' to satisfy audit evidence. No Bank of Canada permit is required for inward capital; the receiving bank will file a large transaction report to FINTRAC if the equivalent is C$10,000 or more. For larger injections, a wire facility with SWIFT gpi tracking is recommended, and the FX conversion is executed at the bank's spot rate on the same value date.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Operating disbursements for AI API platform costs are cleared through the Large Value Transfer System (LVTS) for domestic CAD transfers and through SWIFT MT103 or MT100 on SWIFT gpi for cross-border USD and foreign-currency payments. Commercial Letters of Credit are acceptable under UCP600 where a counterparty requires LC protection, though wholesale AI compute and licensing contracts are typically settled by telegraphic transfer. For USDC-denominated vendor disbursements, the company must route through a FINTRAC-registered digital-asset processor and maintain an audit trail for each fiat-to-stablecoin leg.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: CAD/USD deliverable FX forwards with a Schedule I Canadian bank under an ISDA/CSA master agreement
CAD/USD non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) with an offshore dealer when physical CAD settlement is not required
Cross-currency basis swaps between CAD and USD for long-term asset-liability management
Vanilla CAD/USD FX options for asymmetric liquidity risk management
FX spot transactions with T+2 settlement through CLS for immediate AI API operational inflows

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: CBCA Annual Return (Form 8409, filed electronically via Corporations Canada)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Corporations Canada – Innovation, Science and Economic Development Canada (ISED)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 60 days after the anniversary date of incorporation (the month/day in the articles of incorporation); first return due at first anniversary
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalty of C$100 (approx. USD 75); continued default beyond 1 year authorizes the Director to administratively dissolve the corporation; dissolution terminates operations and assets escheat to the Crown, with costly revival proceedings

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: T2 Corporation Income Tax Return (including Schedules 1–50, Schedule 11 non-resident ownership disclosure, and financial statements if required by CRA)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA), Tax Services Office
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 6 months after the fiscal year-end (e.g., December 31 year-end filed by June 30); balance-due day for unpaid tax is 2 months after year-end (3 months for a Canadian-controlled private corporation claiming the small business deduction)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalty of 5% of unpaid tax plus 1% per full month (maximum 12 months); repeat offender penalty rises to 10% plus 2% per month (maximum 20 months); interest compounded daily at the CRA prescribed rate; arbitrary assessment and denial of loss carry-backs until filed; directors liable for unremitted withholding amounts

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual GST/HST Return (RC59) for the corporation's annual reporting period
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 3 months after the fiscal year-end for annual filers (election permitted if taxable supplies do not exceed C$300,000); instalments, if required, due quarterly
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalty of 1% of the unpaid balance plus 0.25% per complete month (maximum 12 months; minimum C$100); daily compound interest at the prescribed rate; directors jointly and severally liable for unremitted GST/HST (Excise Tax Act s. 323)

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual shareholders' meeting (or unanimous shareholder resolution in lieu) and delivery of annual financial statements to shareholders
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Shareholders; corporate minute book; auditor (if appointed)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: First annual meeting within 18 months of incorporation; thereafter not later than 15 months after the previous annual meeting; financial statements circulated at least 21 days before the meeting
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: No direct monetary penalty; shareholders may apply to court for a compliance order; persistent default can ground Director-initiated dissolution and exposes directors to CBCA s. 122/241 liability for oppression or breach of duty

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Extra-provincial annual renewals in each province where the federal corporation carries on business (e.g., Ontario, British Columbia, Alberta)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Provincial corporate registries (e.g., ServiceOntario, BC Registry, Corporate Registry Alberta)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Anniversary of the extra-provincial registration or province-specific fixed renewal date; Ontario extra-provincial annual return generally due on the registration anniversary
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Revocation or termination of the extra-provincial licence; loss of capacity to enforce contracts and access courts in the province; late-filing fines of up to C$1,000–C$5,000 in certain provinces

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: CBCA ss. 161–163: an independent auditor is mandatory for every distributing (public) corporation; a non-distributing (private) corporation may dispense with an audit each year only by unanimous shareholder resolution and instead obtain a review engagement; no federal revenue, asset, or employee thresholds apply — the distributing/private classification and shareholder unanimity are the sole triggers
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS (CPA Canada Handbook Part I) for distributing corporations; ASPE (Handbook Part II) for private corporations; books and records must be kept in Canada with CRA-compliant working papers; tax payable is computed in CAD unless a functional-currency (USD) election under Income Tax Act s. 261 is made with CRA

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: CBCA ss. 21.1–21.5: maintain a register of individuals with significant control (ISC) reflecting all share transfers and changes in control; update the ISC register within 15 days of any qualifying change; annually reconcile ISC data with the Register of Members at the AGM/anniversary-return cycle; no federal ISC annual filing is currently required (federal beneficial-ownership registry not yet operational); false statements attract fines up to C$1,000,000 and/or 5 years' imprisonment; the register must be produced on demand to shareholders, enforcement agencies, and the Director
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members (with share transfers and issuance history)
Register of Individuals with Significant Control (ISC)
Minute Book (articles, by-laws, minutes, unanimous shareholder agreements)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 110 – 450 per year (C$150–600) for professional registered office and corporate agent services
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 3,800 – 11,500 (review engagement typical for a private AI/LLM platform); USD 11,000 – 37,500 (full CBCA statutory audit)

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 15% federal general corporate income tax rate (Part I, Income Tax Act, RSC 1985, c.1 (5th Supp.)); provincial general rates of 8%–16% apply on top (combined general rate up to ~26.5% in Ontario).
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Small Business Deduction: 9% federal rate on first C$500,000 active business income for CCPCs; SR&ED: 35% fully refundable Investment Tax Credit for qualifying Canadian R&D expenditure for CCPCs (15% non-refundable for large corporations); Patent Box / Innovation and Growth Tax Incentive (proposed Budget 2024, effective 2025): federal rate cut to 10.5% on qualifying patent and AI-related innovation income plus 75% deduction of qualifying IP income; accelerated Capital Cost Allowance (Class 50 / Class 54-55) for computer hardware and software; zero-rating of exported AI/LLM API services under GST/HST s.7(d).
